# Yeasts, moulds and dimorphic fungi

> *Fungi that cause human disease fall into a few groups by growth form, and each group has a typical source and a typical host.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Recognise the main fungi of each group from their growth form, source and host |
| Main organisms | *Candida albicans* (anchor, yeast); *Aspergillus fumigatus* (mould); *Cryptococcus neoformans* (encapsulated yeast) |
| Supporting organisms | Dermatophytes; *Pneumocystis jirovecii*; *Talaromyces marneffei*, a dimorphic fungus of South-East Asia |
| Later in the course | Dermatology, respiratory medicine and the care of immunocompromised patients |
| Scenario questions | Most likely fungus, restricted to the group |
